easy.def: Very mean and fierce.
examples: The vicious dog growled.
The storm was vicious.
The vicious wolf snarled.

more.def: Cruel and likely to hurt others.
examples: The vicious dog snarled at strangers.
A vicious storm tore the roof off the barn.
The villain in the story was vicious.

easy.def: A person who was hurt.
examples: Help came for the storm victims.
The victim of the prank laughed.
The victims got food and blankets.

more.def: A person who has been hurt, harmed or killed by something.
examples: The victims of the flood were given food and blankets.
She was the victim of a prank but laughed it off.
Rescue teams helped the storm victims.

easy.def: A win.
examples: Our team cheered after the victory.
We won! It is a victory!
The victory made us happy.

more.def: The act of winning a game, contest, or battle.
examples: The team's victory was their first of the season.
The crowd cheered the runner's victory.
It was a narrow victory, won by a single point.

easy.def: Moving pictures that you watch on a screen.
examples: We watched a video.
The video is funny.
Dad made a video of the dog.

more.def: A recording of moving pictures and sound that you can watch on a screen.
examples: We watched a video about volcanoes.
She posted a video of her dance.
Dad made a video of our school play.

easy.def: A tape that records pictures and sound.
examples: We watched a videotape.
The videotape is old.
I recorded it on videotape.

more.def: A tape on which moving pictures and sounds are recorded, used for older video players.
examples: We watched the old videotape of my birthday.
The videotape was in a drawer.
The show was recorded on videotape.

easy.def: What you can see from a place.
examples: The view is great.
We have a view of the lake.
The view from the hill is pretty.

more.def: What you can see from a particular place.
examples: We had a view of the whole valley from the top.
The room has a view of the ocean.
The view from the hill was beautiful.

easy.def: What you think about something.
examples: In my view, pizza is best.
What is your view?
He has a different view.

more.def: A way of thinking about something.
examples: In my view, dogs make the best pets.
She shared her view on the plan.
They have different views about the game.

easy.def: A very small town.
examples: My grandma lives in a village.
The village has one little shop.
We walked to the village.

more.def: A small group of houses and buildings, smaller than a town.
examples: The village had one school, one shop, and a tiny post office.
Fishing boats lined the shore of the village.
Everyone in the village knows each other.

easy.def: A bad person in a story.
examples: The villain was mean.
The hero beat the villain.
The villain wore black.

more.def: A bad character in a story who causes trouble for the hero.
examples: The villain tried to trick the hero.
In the movie, the villain stole the gold.
The villain had a sneaky laugh.

easy.def: To break a rule or law.
examples: Do not violate the rules.
He violated the law.
The car violated the speed limit.

more.def: To break a rule, promise or law.
examples: Do not violate the school rules.
The driver violated the speed limit.
The player violated the rules of the game.

easy.def: Breaking a rule.
examples: Running in the hall is a violation.
The violation was minor.
The driver got a violation.

more.def: An act of breaking a rule, law or promise.
examples: Running in the hall is a violation of the rules.
The driver got a ticket for a parking violation.
The violation was reported to the teacher.

easy.def: Hurting people or things with force.
examples: Violence is wrong.
The movie had no violence.
Fighting is violence.

more.def: Behavior that uses force to hurt people or break things.
examples: The teacher talked about stopping violence in our town.
Many people work to end violence and build peace.
Violence is never a good way to solve a problem.

easy.def: Using strong force that can hurt.
examples: The storm was violent.
A violent wind blew.
The waves were violent.

more.def: Very rough and strong, and likely to hurt or damage something.
examples: A violent storm broke the tree.
The violent waves crashed on the rocks.
The film was too violent for little kids.

easy.def: A small musical instrument with strings that you play with a bow.
examples: I play the violin.
The violin makes a high sound.
She holds the violin.

more.def: A musical instrument with four strings that is held under the chin and played with a bow.
examples: She plays the violin in the school orchestra.
The violin sang a sweet tune.
He tuned his violin before the concert.

easy.def: A tiny germ that can make you sick.
examples: A virus gave me a cold.
The doctor said I have a virus.
A virus is a very small germ.

more.def: A tiny germ that makes people, animals or plants sick.
examples: Doctors study how a virus spreads from one person to another.
Washing your hands helps stop a virus from spreading.
Doctors found out which virus made the flu.

easy.def: Your sight.
examples: My vision is clear.
Good vision.
He has poor vision.

more.def: The ability to see.
examples: Eagles have sharp vision.
My vision is blurry without glasses.
She had her vision checked.

easy.def: Something you picture in your mind.
examples: She had a vision of the future.
A vision of home.
He saw a vision in his dream.

more.def: A picture in the mind of something that could be.
examples: She had a vision of a beautiful garden.
He saw a vision of home in his dream.
The leader shared her vision for the town.

easy.def: To go see a person or a place.
examples: We visit Grandma.
I visited the zoo.
They visit us every year.

more.def: To go and spend time with a person or at a place.
examples: We visited the science museum on Saturday.
My cousins visit us every summer.
She visited her grandmother in the hospital.

easy.def: A time when you go see someone.
examples: We had a visit from Grandma.
The visit was fun.
My visit to the dentist was short.

more.def: A time spent with a person or in a place.
examples: We enjoyed a visit from our cousins.
Our class made a visit to the farm.
Her visit to the museum lasted all day.

easy.def: A person who comes to see you or a place.
examples: We have a visitor at our house.
The visitor rang the bell.
Our class had a visitor today.

more.def: A person who goes to see someone or to spend time in a place.
examples: Visitors to the park must stay on the trails.
The new baby had many visitors at the hospital.
A visitor from Japan spoke to our class.

easy.def: Having to do with seeing.
examples: A picture is a visual aid.
The visual art was bright.
The visual display was fun.

more.def: Having to do with what you can see.
examples: A map is a visual aid that helps you find places.
The painting was a visual treat.
The class made a visual display of the planets.

easy.def: Very important.
examples: Water is vital.
It is vital to wear a seat belt.
Sleep is vital.

more.def: Needed for life, or very important.
examples: Water is vital for all living things.
Vital supplies were flown to the town after the flood.
The bridge is a vital link between the towns.
